what_was_said: That CEMLA lived at cemla.org
what_is_true: cemla.org is a Mexican central-banking body. The arrivals index is at cemla.com/buscador/
how_it_was_caught: David went to the address given and found the wrong institution.

what_was_said: That Mary Ann Hellen Brayley was a new find
what_is_true: She had been in data/taylor-line.tsv since 8 September, from David's own MyHeritage tree. What findmypast supplied was a citation - the baptism of 30 Oct 1884 at Northam, ref 1843A/PR/1/16 - not the fact.
how_it_was_caught: David: "why is her mothers name new? its been in my myheritage tree forever."

what_was_said: That the Rosario marriage index showed "Larena V x Sarmiento A" at Libro 9 folio 20 - and that this was a candidate
what_is_true: The entry reads *** LAVENA V. x BELMONTE A. ***. It was misread at low resolution and kept a false candidate alive for two days.
how_it_was_caught: Read again at the film's maximum resolution on 10 September. Not close: the hand is unambiguous.

what_was_said: That a cluster of Larena/Lerena at Cayasta might be a kindred
what_is_true: Cayasta is an ITALIAN colony - Laurini five times, Lauron, Castelarin - and the same mother is transcribed Azela in one act and Raiela in another. The "cluster" was a transcription artefact.
how_it_was_caught: Reading the acts instead of the index. Retracted publicly; the register entry is now EXCLUDED.

what_was_said: That the 1869 census showed a Llerena HOUSEHOLD at Rosario
what_is_true: The image shows twelve separately-numbered, unrelated individuals in a conventillo. There is ONE man of the name, Bartolome, not a family.
how_it_was_caught: Opening the image instead of trusting the index grouping.

what_was_said: That Gabino L. Llerena was a Rosario-born link between the two countries
what_is_true: Every other person on his record is Uruguayan, so the Rosario in question is Rosario, COLONIA, in Uruguay.
how_it_was_caught: Caught before it was published, by reading the rest of the record.

what_was_said: That reading the Rosario registers needed the Chrome extension, because the in-app browser could not crop
what_is_true: Wrong twice. The viewer has its own zoom, and - far more important - the Image Index panel is an HTML TABLE. The handwriting never needed to be read at all.
how_it_was_caught: David: "why do you need chrome? use your own browser?"

what_was_said: That "Armand[o] Lorena", born 1882 at Rosario de Lerma, Salta, was "probably not him" - written off on four objections
what_is_true: It IS him. The image reads "Clase de 1882 / LERENA - Pablo Armando / hijo de JUAN CARLOS LERENA y de MARIA LERENA / Nacido en Rosario de Santa Fe / Oficina enroladora de CAPETOWN". Three of the four objections were artefacts of a machine index that dropped "Pablo", moved him 1,400 km, wrote Lerena as Lorena, and invented the surname "Serena" out of the printed word SERIE.
how_it_was_caught: Opening the image. It took two minutes. *** This is the most serious error in the archive: the central finding of the project was nearly discarded. ***

what_was_said: That Roque's first wife was "Rosalina Wilhelmina CHAPPELL", read from a marriage index
what_is_true: CHAPPELL was her MARRIED name. She was Roseline Wilhelmina FORBES, widow of Frederick Christian Chappell. The 1936 register calls her "Rosaline Wilhermina Forbes Chappell" because that is what a remarrying widow is called.
how_it_was_caught: The 1920 Chappell-Forbes marriage, found in BOTH the civil and the Anglican registers, plus Chappell's own estate file.

what_was_said: Margin readings taken from register openings rendered at 42% scale
what_is_true: Not reliable. At that size "Timoteo Lucero" was read as "Armando Sara" - both words wrong, and an L-surname missed, which is the exact failure that matters when hunting one L-surname. Every opening was re-read from the margin strips at maximum resolution.
how_it_was_caught: Zooming on a single doubtful entry, and finding it was not doubtful at all - it was simply wrong.

what_was_said: That the Lerena palette was identical to the FALCO archive's, with hex values quoted
what_is_true: The values quoted were Falco's, not ours. The Lerena styles.css is byte-identical to the DEFRANCESKI archive's. Falco is the outlier, with a warm palette against the shared cool one.
how_it_was_caught: Reading both files side by side instead of trusting memory.

what_was_said: That there were 29 places in the register
what_is_true: 28. "arr. Buenos Aires 1907-07-14" had been sitting as its own one-person place beside the 43-person "Buenos Aires - arrivals" because the normalising pattern only matched "arr. YYYY".
how_it_was_caught: Looking at a person page that had no business having its own place.

what_was_said: Layout: a bare "6" floating in the middle of a sentence on every person page
what_is_true:
.prose is a flex COLUMN, not a paragraph class. Using it on a

made every inline its own row.
how_it_was_caught: Looking at the rendered page rather than the built HTML.

what_was_said: That the Italian-origin hypothesis was "the most consequential thing on this page"
what_is_true: Within the hour, the low-confidence genetic groups showed no Italian group among the five legible ones - evidence against it. Downgraded the same day to "already weaker than when it was written".
how_it_was_caught: The next screenshot.

what_was_said: That the four LERINA arrivals of 1889 were excluded because "LERINA here is an Italian surname, not a variant of the Spanish Lerena"
what_is_true: They ARE excluded, but on their dates and the composition of the party: they arrive in 1889 aged 59, 55, 21 and 17, seven years after Pablo Armando was born at Rosario, and the party contains no Juan Carlos and no Maria. The claim about the SURNAME is withdrawn as a reason - it was reached from an index without opening the manifest, which is the move that got the Armando Lorena card wrong.
how_it_was_caught: This archive's own search box, which showed all four LERINA entries carrying the same unexamined label.

what_was_said: That the Arturo Lerena in army drawer Cajon 985 was born at Montevideo in 1858, son of Avelino Lerena and Ambrosia Traibel
what_is_true: Two men. The Uruguayan record relied on gives the wife as EMA REGULES, and Ema Regules married JUAN ARTURO Lerena Traibel (1861-1936), whose children were born at Montevideo 1881-87. The Arturo in the drawer married AMALIA DIAZ and had children in La Pampa, Mendoza and Entre Rios 1889-97. The row is withdrawn and a "four branches" claim became three.
how_it_was_caught: Opening the FamilySearch Tree profile the record was attached to - going to the underlying record, which is the move this archive keeps having to relearn.

what_was_said: Every person page showed an empty children list unless somebody had separately written an explicit "child" row
what_is_true: A link is written once in data/relations.tsv - "X, father, Y" - and the builder recorded it on X's page and never reversed it onto Y's. Thirty-eight parent edges were read one way against fifteen compensating child rows. Pablo Armando, Juan Carlos, Maria Lerena, Mary Septima Taylor, Roque, Roseline Forbes and Doreen Chappell all had children in the data and none on their charts. Fixed in the builder, with aliases excluded so a machine-index variant is not counted as a second child.
how_it_was_caught: Wiring in the Montevideo household, whose four documented children rendered as none.

what_was_said: Nothing, visibly - which is why it went unnoticed
what_is_true: The people builder looked people up by name, and ELEVEN NAMES appeared twice or three times in the register - three Francisco Lerenas, three Jose Llerenas, two Carlos Lerenas, two Gilbertos. The later row silently won and thirteen rows could not be addressed at all. No edge happened to name an ambiguous person, so nothing looked wrong - but the next edge added would have attached to the wrong man in silence. Duplicates now carry a distinguishing tag and the builder REFUSES TO BUILD if two rows share a name.
how_it_was_caught: Caught on the way to adding twenty-four relationship edges, several of them to a "Carlos LERENA" and a "Gilberto LERENA".

what_was_said: "Of the 1 relationships in the chart above"
what_is_true: A plural where the count can be one. Three people pages carried it.
how_it_was_caught: An audit of all 138 person pages after the chart builder was changed.

what_was_said: 129 people in the register
what_is_true: 138, and climbing. The figure was typed by hand, correct when written and stale within days. It now derives from the data, like everything else on this site - the whole method being that pages are generated from the TSVs so page and data cannot drift. This one had escaped it.
how_it_was_caught: Reading the front page instead of assuming it.
